properties.title: Wake in the Closet
properties.text:
You wake up on the quilt under the stairs. The coats sway though there's no wind.
Through the floorboards, the clink of plates. Dad is setting the table.
Dad: Up, boy. Supper's getting cold, and so is your mother.

properties.title: Supper with Dad
properties.text:
Dad sits at the head of the table. Across from him, the Effigy, its sack head turned slightly toward you.
Dad: Sit. Eat. Your mother's watching.
You eat the gray soup. It tastes like pennies.
Dad: The Last Supper is coming. The sabbath. When it's laid out, this house will be consecrated, and she'll be whole.
Dad: But the dust is getting thicker. I need to see farther in the dark.
Dad: Out in the corn there's a battery, a wire, and a mirror. Bring them to me and I'll make you a flashlight.
Dad: You'll have ten minutes before the Night Crusher comes for you. Don't make him carry you home.

properties.title: Dad on the Night Crusher
properties.text:
Boy: Who is the Night Crusher?
Dad: He keeps the yard. He keeps the hours. He's not cruel, but he's very strong.
Dad: He hears footfalls, not voices. When the ground shakes, stop. Walk on your toes. Breathe through your nose.
Dad: Do that and he'll pass you by.

properties.title: Out the Back Door
properties.text:
The back door swings shut behind you. The dust is so thick it tastes like chalk.
The orange glow sits low on the horizon. It's dimmer than it was yesterday.
Far away across the field, a white house is lit up like a lantern. You've never been able to reach it.
Ahead, the corn begins.

properties.title: The Crash
properties.text:
The rows open into a clearing. In the middle, a pileup of old cars has rusted into a single heap.
Scarecrows lie everywhere, crushed under fenders, tangled in axles, as if they all ran here at once.
Somewhere in this mess are the battery, the wire, and the mirror.

properties.title: The Pickup
properties.text:
The pickup's door hangs by one hinge. Behind the cracked dashboard, a heavy battery is still bolted in.
You work it loose. It's warm, like it's been sitting in the sun, though there is no sun.

properties.title: Under the Sedan
properties.text:
You wriggle under the sedan on your belly. A scarecrow's arm is pinned beside you, its straw fingers curled.
A length of copper wire dangles from the engine. You pull until it snaps free.

properties.title: The Scarecrow Pile
properties.text:
You dig through gray straw and rotten overalls. Some of the scarecrows are wearing wedding rings.
At the bottom, clutched in a burlap hand, a small round mirror.
You look into it. For a moment, your face isn't there.
Then it is.

properties.title: Not Yet
properties.text:
You think of Dad's face if you come home with empty hands.
You're still missing something.

outcomes.label: A Hole in the Earth
outcomes.description: You find a dark opening between the rows

outcomes.label: Footsteps Behind You
outcomes.description: The stalks start to bend toward you

properties.title: The Burrow Mouth
properties.text:
Between two rows, the ground falls away into a tunnel big enough for something much larger than you.
A coal-red glow pulses deep inside. The walls are scored with long, even furrows, like fingers dragged through clay.
The air coming up smells like a cellar. This is where he lives.
You back away slowly.

nodes.title: Do You Know How to Tiptoe?

properties.title: Do You Know How to Tiptoe?
Holding Your Breath
properties.text:
You stop. Toes. Nose. The battery is heavy in your arms.
A blank clay face rises above the corn, turns one way, then the other.
It sinks back down. The footsteps fade toward the burrow.
You run the rest of the way.

properties.title: The Night Crusher
properties.text:
The corn parts. A hand the size of a wagon wheel closes around you.
It isn't rough. It's patient.
Night Crusher: Time.
The ground opens and you go down with him into the dark.

properties.title: Below the Yard
properties.text:
You wake on a thin pallet with a clean white sheet. Coal glows in the wall.
The Night Crusher sits hunched in the corner with his back to you, like he's giving you privacy.
Down here you don't feel tired anymore. Just very small.
Night Crusher: Rest. Then up you go.

properties.title: The House Is Bigger
properties.text:
You wake on the quilt under the stairs. You feel worn thin, like a shirt washed too many times.
The hallway outside the closet is longer than it was. There's a new door at the end of it.
Behind the door, a boy is crying. He sounds like you.
You reach for the knob. The door slams in your face.
Dad: Back out, boy. The corn's still waiting.

properties.title: The Flashlight
properties.text:
You stumble in the back door, coated in dust, arms full.
Dad lays the battery, the wire, and the mirror on the table beside the Effigy's empty plate.
His soot-black fingers twist and solder. A beam of white light cuts through the dust in the room.
Dad: Good job. This is your flashlight. Use it sparingly, because the dark notices light.
He turns the beam across the Effigy's blank burlap face.
Dad: Your mother needs eyes. And teeth. We'll talk about that tomorrow.

properties.title: The Open Grave
properties.text:
Ten rows in, the corn stops around a fresh hole in the ground.
It's a grave, dug neat and square. The dirt piled beside it is still dark and wet.
There's no headstone. Down at the bottom, something pale is half-buried.

nodes.title: The grave is right at your feet.

properties.title: The grave is right at your feet.
Into the Grave
properties.text:
You drop down into the grave. The walls are higher than your head.
The pale thing is a child's shoe, laced up tight. There's nothing in it.
The ground hums under your hands, the way it does when something heavy walks nearby.
You dig your fingers into the wall and climb out.

properties.title: The Cow Carcass
properties.text:
A cow lies dead across the row. Its ribs stand up like the frame of a barn after a fire.
The hide has gone stiff and gray. Flies drone in the hollow where its belly used to be.
The smell reaches you before you reach it.

properties.title: The Smell
properties.text:
You lean in close and breathe.
Under the rot there's something else: coal smoke, and wet clay. A cellar smell.
You've smelled it before, on your own quilt, on mornings you don't remember coming home.
Behind you, the corn creaks.

properties.title: The Barking Dog
properties.text:
A thin yellow dog stands in the middle of the row, barking and barking.
Its ribs show, and there's a rope around its neck that isn't tied to anything.
It doesn't run at you. It barks past you, at something in the corn behind your back.

properties.title: Good Dog
properties.text:
You hold out your hand. The dog stops barking and pushes its head under your palm.
Its fur is full of dust, and it's shaking.
Then it pulls away, whines once, and bolts into the rows.
The silence afterward is very loud.

properties.title: The Mailbox
properties.text:
The rows end at a dirt road. A tin mailbox leans on a post at its edge, out here where no one lives.
The flag is up. Painted on the side, in Dad's careful letters, is your family's name.
Past the road, the corn opens up. You can hear metal ticking as it cools.

Boy.info: A four-year-old in an oversized flannel nightshirt and scuffed boots, hair full of dust, eyes too large for his narrow face. He is small enough to slip between cornstalks and under car wrecks. Rendered as a simple bold silhouette, pale against the dark.

Dad.info: A tall, gaunt man in a stained leather apron over a Depression-era waistcoat, sleeves rolled to the elbow, forearms blackened with soot. Round smoked-glass spectacles hide his eyes. He moves little and speaks as if reciting scripture or a recipe. Half father, half warlock-alchemist.

Effigy.info: A crude life-size figure of the Boy's missing mother propped in a high-backed chair. Its body is a dress form stuffed with straw and wrapped in a faded floral housedress. The head is a burlap sack with no features yet. Empty spaces where eyes, teeth and hands should be are marked with pins and chalk.

Night Crusher.info: A hulking chthonic shape, taller than the cornstalks, made of packed earth, root and coal dust, with a long stooped back. Its face is a smooth blank of clay with a single horizontal crack. It drags one enormous hand along the ground and leaves a furrow behind it. It is seen mostly in silhouette, black against black.

The Closet.info: A narrow coat closet under the stairs where the Boy sleeps on a folded quilt. Moth-eaten coats hang overhead like sleeping bats. A thin blade of yellow light comes under the door. The walls feel slightly farther apart each time he wakes.

Dining Room.info: A long farmhouse table under a single bare bulb, set with mismatched plates and a tureen of something gray. Dust sifts constantly through the window frames. At the head of the table sits Dad, and across from him sits the Effigy. Alchemical glassware crowds the sideboard.

Back Field.info: A flat expanse of Dust Bowl Kansas behind the house, black and white like an old photograph, with dust hanging in the air like fog. A dim orange glow sits on the horizon. Very far off, impossibly bright, a gleaming white house stands alone in the field. It never seems to get closer.

Corn Maze.info: High dead corn and wheat, taller than a man, rattling in the wind, with narrow rows that twist back on themselves. Scarecrows stand at odd intervals, some tilted, some face-down. Visibility is a few feet at most. Pools of faint light come from nowhere in particular.

The Crash.info: A clearing at the heart of the maze where several 1930s cars have collided and rusted together into one heap: a pickup, a sedan, a delivery truck on its side. Dozens of scarecrows are piled and crushed among the wreckage, their straw gone gray, as if they have been out here for years.

Night Crusher's Burrow.info: A low earthen chamber beneath the yard, lit by a smoldering coal seam in the wall. Roots hang from the ceiling. In one corner lies a thin pallet with a clean white sheet, oddly cared-for. It is quiet down here, like being inside a held breath.

projectTitle: Night of the Night Crusher (Choice Maze)
